Facebook pages, and the Instagram business accounts linked to them.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Facebook Pages account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/apps)
- **Settings:** `FACEBOOK_APP_ID`, `FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET`
- **Added with:** `everyapp provider add --oauth facebook`

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/facebook/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `everyapp provider show facebook` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

A Business app with Facebook Login. Meta issues no refresh token: a person reconnects when the token expires. Not yet tried against a live connect.

1. Open [developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/apps) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Allow the scopes behind the sets your apps use (the table below), and no others.
4. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Facebook%20Pages) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
everyapp provider add --oauth facebook
everyapp secret set FACEBOOK_APP_ID FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Facebook account (who you are) | `public_profile` |
| `pages.read` | Pages you manage and their insights (read) | `pages_show_list`, `pages_read_engagement`, `read_insights` |
| `pages.write` | Pages you manage (read, post and reply) | `pages_show_list`, `business_management`, `pages_manage_posts`, `pages_manage_engagement`, `pages_read_engagement` |
| `instagram.write` | Instagram business accounts linked to your pages | `pages_show_list`, `instagram_basic`, `instagram_content_publish`, `instagram_manage_comments`, `instagram_manage_insights` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  facebook: { access: "read", scopes: ["pages.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `everyapp provider show facebook` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Facebook Pages**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
